work_order.understanding:
The per-occurrence identity of a posted schedule is the pair (schedule, schedule_occurrence) written by postTransactionForSchedule. Before writing, that handler checks whether the occurrence is already spent (packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:585-597): inside the `if (!today)` block it queries `q('transactions').filter({ schedule, schedule_occurrence: occurrence }).select('id')`. That query carries no `.options({ splits })`, so AQL defaults to `inline` (packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema/executors.ts:51-55) and execTransactionsBasic appends `is_parent = 0` (executors.ts:238-244). A split parent is exactly the row the stamp survives on: splitTransaction keeps the original row, sets is_parent: true and clears its payee (packages/loot-core/src/shared/transactions.ts:405-412), while makeChild copies neither `schedule` nor `schedule_occurrence` (transactions.ts:57-82). So the one row carrying the stamp is the one row the guard cannot see, and the occurrence looks unspent. getHasTransactionsQuery (shared/schedules.ts:218-219) and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery (schedules.ts:252-253) both already pass splits: 'all', so the guard is the only one of the three that does not — which is why the Schedules page reads an occurrence as paid while a second post for it still writes.

I reproduced this on this checkout by running the real handler sequence, not from the ticket's account of it: a monthly schedule, occurrence 2016-12-02, posted once then split through splitTransaction + makeEmptySplitSubtransactions applied via the transactions-batch-update handler, then posted again for the same occurrence, leaves TWO rows stamped 2016-12-02 — split parent id7 and a fresh id10, both -10000. Adding `.options({ splits: 'all' })` and re-running leaves exactly one (id7). I also confirmed the direction is safe rather than merely different: a split parent stamped for occurrence A does not block occurrence B, a genuinely still-owed later date, from posting (both rows appear, 2016-12-02 and 2017-01-02); and the `today` path still writes twice, unchanged.

ON THE PRIOR PLAN REVIEW — the change it asked for is applied, but its stated reason is factually wrong and the implementer must not encode it. The review objected that AC-1's observable ('exactly one transaction for that payee and date — the split parent') names a state that cannot exist, because the split parent's payee column is null, so the count comes out 0 in the collapsed register and 2 in the expanded one. The payee column really is null — I confirmed it: parent id7 after the split is {payee: null, is_parent: true}. But the register does not render a split parent's payee from that column. PayeeCell renders `useDisplayPayee({ transaction })` (packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.tsx:668), and DisplayPayeeProvider derives a parent's display payee from its CHILDREN's most common payee (packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useDisplayPayee.tsx:96-140). I rendered the real TransactionsTable with a persisted split parent (payee null) plus two children carrying a payee, and the payee cell contains 'Alice' and the Category cell contains 'Split'. So the review's conclusion is right — the payee-count wording is fragile because it means different things in the two expansion states, and it reads the DB shape rather than the screen — while its evidence for it is not. The observable has been restated in the Split-marker formulation the review required, which is stable in both states; what changed is the reason, not the requirement. Nobody should expect a blank payee cell on a split parent, and no comment, test name, or how_to_verify in this change should say a split parent's payee cell is blank.
work_order.root_cause: The duplicate-occurrence guard in postTransactionForSchedule (packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:585-597) queries q('transactions') with no .options({ splits: ... }). AQL defaults 'transactions' to splits: 'inline', which appends `is_parent = 0` and excludes split parents. Since splitTransaction retains the schedule and schedule_occurrence stamp on the parent row only (makeChild copies neither), the guard sees no stamped row after a split and the occurrence looks unspent. getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery both already pass splits: 'all', so the guard is the sole outlier of the three and is the only one of them that can disagree with the status the Schedules page renders.
work_order.approach: One-line widening of the guard's row set, matching the two sibling queries that already answer the same question, plus the tests the issue asks for. Insert .options({ splits: 'all' }) into the alreadyPosted guard query inside the `if (!today)` block so it sees the split parent carrying the stamp. The `today` branch stays unguarded — it pays next_date early and deliberately leaves the occurrence pending — and is untouched, because the guard lives entirely inside `if (!today)`. Children are not matched by the widened filter: makeChild copies neither field, so they cannot carry the stamp and cannot newly trigger the guard. The explanatory comment above the guard gains a note on why 'all' is required, because the default is the trap: a reader who simplifies it away reintroduces a money bug with no type error. Tests go in the existing `consuming an occurrence twice` describe block of app.test.ts, whose helpers (post, createWeeklySchedule) the new cases reuse. The split is driven through the real path rather than by hand-inserting an is_parent row, so a test failure is attributable to the guard's query rather than to the stamp having been lost by the split. Note for the implementer: getTransactionDates() and readPostedTransaction() in that file query with the default 'inline' splits and return zero rows for a split parent — I confirmed this (an inline query over a split-parented schedule returned only the newly written row, not the parent) — so post-split assertions must query with .options({ splits: 'all' }) explicitly.

files.change: In postTransactionForSchedule, inside the `if (!today)` block at lines 585-597, insert `.options({ splits: 'all' })` between `q('transactions')` and `.filter({ schedule: schedule.id, schedule_occurrence: occurrence })` at line 589, so the guard reads `q('transactions').options({ splits: 'all' }).filter({ ... }).select('id')`. Append to the comment block immediately above the guard (lines 572-584) a short paragraph stating that 'all' is required because splitTransaction keeps the schedule and schedule_occurrence stamp on the parent row and makeChild copies neither, so the default 'inline' (is_parent = 0) excludes the only row carrying the stamp; that the option matches getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery, which already pass it, so the guard and the status queries agree on whether an occurrence is posted; and that this cannot over-block, since children never carry the stamp so the widened filter matches no row the previous filter did not. Do not change the `today` branch, the filter's fields, the select, or the `alreadyPosted != null` early return.
files.why: This is the whole fix and the only place the guard lives. Verified by execution on this checkout: without it a post/split/post sequence leaves two stamped transactions; with it, exactly one, while a still-owed later occurrence still posts.

cases: In the `consuming an occurrence twice` describe block: post an occurrence, split the resulting transaction through the real path (splitTransaction from #shared/transactions with makeEmptySplitSubtransactions, applied through the transactions-batch-update handler on #server/transactions/app), then post the SAME occurrence again — assert exactly one row carries that schedule and schedule_occurrence. Query with .options({ splits: 'all' }); getTransactionDates() uses the default 'inline' splits and returns zero rows for a split parent, so it cannot be used as-is here.

In the same block: assert the split parent itself retains the stamp (schedule and schedule_occurrence both equal the occurrence) and that the children do NOT (makeChild copies neither), so a failure of the case above is attributable to the guard's query rather than to the stamp having been lost or propagated by the split.

In the same block: the pre-existing case 'writes one transaction when posted twice in sequence' (no split in between) must still pass unchanged — the widening must not have broken the case it was already covering. Baseline for this file on this checkout, before any change: 48 tests, all passing.

New case, the over-blocking direction: a monthly schedule whose occurrence A has been posted and split must still allow a genuinely different, still-owed occurrence B to post. Assert both rows exist afterwards, stamped A and B respectively, and that exactly one row carries B's occurrence. Verified on this checkout that this holds with the fix applied. This fails if the guard is ever widened to something coarser than an exact stamp match.
Existing case that must keep passing: 'does not guard `today`, which may legitimately be posted twice' — the `today` path deliberately stays unguarded and writes twice; the fix must not reach it.

acceptance.check: On a one-off schedule, posting the occurrence, splitting the resulting transaction in the account register, and then choosing 'Post transaction' on that schedule again leaves exactly one row for that date carrying the Split marker in its Category cell — the split parent — and adds no second, un-split transaction row for that occurrence. Before this change the register shows the split parent AND a second un-split row with the same payee, date and amount.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Boot with `yarn start` and use 'View demo' on the setup screen. On /schedules add a new one-off schedule: payee, account, amount, date a few days out. Open that row's actions menu and choose 'Post transaction' (NOT 'Post transaction today' — `today` is deliberately unguarded and must keep writing twice). Note the transaction in the register: one row carrying that payee and date. Select it, click its Category cell, choose 'Split'. The register now shows that row carrying the Split marker in its Category cell. Return to /schedules and choose 'Post transaction' again on the same row. The register must still show exactly ONE row for that date carrying the Split marker, and no second un-split row beside it. Count the Split marker, not the payee: a split parent keeps the Split marker in both the collapsed and the expanded state, whereas how many rows carry the payee depends on which state you are in (collapsed: one row; expanded: the parent plus its children). Do not expect the split parent's payee cell to be blank — the register derives it from the split's children, so it shows the payee.

acceptance.check: A split parent stamped for one occurrence does not mark a different, still-owed occurrence of the same schedule as paid: posting that later occurrence afterwards still writes its transaction.

Not a browser check: it needs two occurrences of one schedule with a specific split in between, which is faster and less flaky to assert directly.

I confirmed on this checkout that both queries do return the stamped parent after a split, so a regression in any of the three is attributable. Not a browser check: the disagreement is between three queries, and no screen renders it as a distinct observable state.

acceptance.check: The post-then-split-then-post case has a permanent regression test, and the full loot-core schedules suite still passes with the widened guard.

qa_script: Boot with `yarn start` (port 3001) and, on the setup screen, choose 'View demo' so the budget has accounts and sample data rather than being empty.

Go to /schedules and add a new ONE-OFF schedule (a single date, not a recurring rule): pick a payee, an account, an amount, and a date a few days out. One-off matters — a recurring schedule's next_date advances after a post, so 'Post transaction' would target a different occurrence and prove nothing. I confirmed server-side that a one-off's next_date does not move after a post, so the second 'Post transaction' re-dispatches the same occurrence.

Open that row's actions menu and choose 'Post transaction'. Do NOT choose 'Post transaction today': `today` deliberately pays early, leaves the occurrence pending, and is meant to be re-postable. Choosing it would produce two transactions even after this fix and read as a regression.
Open the account's register and confirm exactly one transaction for that payee and date.

Select that transaction and click its Category cell; choose 'Split' from the dropdown. The register now shows that row carrying the Split marker in its Category cell. Note that its payee cell still shows the payee — that is correct, not a bug; the register derives a split parent's payee from its children.
Return to /schedules, open the SAME row's actions menu, and choose 'Post transaction' again.

Go back to the register: there must still be exactly ONE row for that date carrying the Split marker, and no second un-split row beside it. A second un-split row with the same payee, date and amount is the bug. Judge this on the Split marker rather than on the payee count: the Split marker is on exactly one row whether the split is collapsed or expanded, while the payee appears on one row collapsed and on the parent plus its children expanded — so a payee count gives a different answer in each state and will read as a pass or a fail depending only on which state you happen to be in.

Negative control, to prove the setup can actually produce two rows: with the same one-off schedule, post it once WITHOUT splitting, then choose 'Post transaction' again from /schedules. Even before this change that yields one row — confirm it, so step 7's single row is evidence about the split and not about a menu item that never worked.

Adversarial pass, the direction the fix could plausibly over-reach: on a RECURRING schedule, post the first occurrence from the register's Upcoming section, split that transaction, then post the SECOND occurrence from Upcoming. The second occurrence must still post and appear — if a split on one occurrence ever made the next occurrence read as paid, this change has over-blocked.
risks: Money, on the write path: this is the guard that decides whether one occurrence of a schedule can be paid twice, and the change widens the row set that guard matches. The direction is safe — a broader guard sees more rows, never fewer, and the rows it newly sees are precisely those carrying the stamp — but it is the kind of widening that must not be widened further by a later reader.

The default is the trap. Omitting .options({ splits: ... }) on a 'transactions' query is valid AQL and silently means 'inline', which excludes split parents. A future edit that simplifies the query back loses this fix with no type error and no failing test other than the new split case. The comment added above the guard is load-bearing for that reason.

Test helpers in the same file silently disagree about splits: getTransactionDates() and readPostedTransaction() query with the default 'inline' and report zero rows for a split parent. Reusing either for a post-split assertion would make a correct implementation look broken. The new tests query with .options({ splits: 'all' }) explicitly.

The prior plan review's stated reason for its required change was wrong (it held that a split parent's payee cell renders blank; it renders the payee, derived from the children — confirmed by rendering TransactionsTable). The required change has been applied anyway because it is independently correct, but if the implementer finds prose anywhere in this repo asserting a split parent's payee cell is blank, that prose is wrong and should not be propagated into a test name or a comment.
The change touches no path in forbidden_paths and adds no dependency, no new host, and no network call — nothing in env.api_allowlist is involved.
out_of_scope: Splitting a posted occurrence still leaves the stamp only on the parent row, never on the children. That is what makes this bug possible, but moving or copying the stamp onto children would change what a split means for schedules and is not what the issue asks for; the guard is fixed to read the row that already carries it.

Unsplitting a posted-and-split transaction drops the stamp entirely, so an occurrence whose payment was split and then unsplit can be posted again. That is a separate question about the stamp's lifecycle with a different fix; it would ship on its own if this ticket did not exist.

Merging transactions and transferring them already carry schedule_occurrence explicitly (packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/merge.ts:174,186 and transfer.ts:69,136) and already pass splits: 'all' where they query. No change needed there.

No UI change. Both surfaces named in the issue — the register's Upcoming section and the Schedules page menu — dispatch the same schedule/post-transaction handler, and both are correct once the guard is; the register's dispatch passes an explicit date (Account.tsx:1567) and the Schedules page menu does not (SchedulesTable.tsx:184), which is why the QA script uses a one-off schedule for the page path.
The `today` branch of postTransactionForSchedule stays unguarded by design and is not changed.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The defect was reproduced on this checkout by running the real handler sequence rather than taken from the ticket's description; the one-line fix was applied and confirmed to collapse two stamped rows to one; the over-blocking direction was checked explicitly (a split on occurrence A still lets occurrence B post) and the `today` path confirmed unchanged; both status queries were confirmed to still see the split parent after the split. The 143 tests across the schedules, shared-schedules and forecast suites pass at baseline. The register's rendering of a split parent was confirmed by rendering TransactionsTable with a persisted split, not by clicking through a running app, so the residual 10% is the end-to-end browser walkthrough in AC-1 and the possibility that the Split affordance has moved in the UI — the plan traces the Category-cell dropdown as its location.
evidence: Without the fix: post occurrence 2016-12-02, split it through splitTransaction + makeEmptySplitSubtransactions via the transactions-batch-update handler, post again -> TWO rows stamped 2016-12-02 (split parent id7 {payee: null, is_parent: true, amount: -10000} and fresh id10 {payee: id3, amount: -10000}). An inline-splits query over the same schedule returns only id10 — the parent is invisible to the default the guard uses.
With .options({ splits: 'all' }) added to the guard: the identical script leaves exactly one row (id7, is_parent true, stamped 2016-12-02).

Over-blocking check with the fix applied: monthly schedule, occurrence 2016-12-02 posted then split, then 2017-01-02 posted -> both rows present, distinct occurrences. The widened guard does not make a still-owed occurrence read as paid.
`today` path with the fix applied: posted twice with today: true -> still two rows, both stamped 2017-01-02, dated 2017-01-01. The branch is untouched.

One-off schedule via the Schedules-page dispatch shape (post with no date argument, which is what SchedulesTable.tsx:184 sends): next_date stays 2016-12-05 after the first post, so the second 'Post transaction' re-dispatches the same occurrence; post, split, post again leaves two stamped rows without the fix.

Status-query agreement with the fix applied: getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery each return the stamped parent row (id7, 2016-12-02) after the split, before and after alike.

Register rendering, tested by rendering the real TransactionsTable with a persisted split (parent payee null, is_parent true) and two children carrying a payee: collapsed state gives payee cells ['Alice'] and category cells ['Split']; expanded gives payee cells ['Alice','Alice','Alice'] and category cells ['Split','Categorize','Categorize']. So the Split marker is on exactly one row in BOTH states, while the payee count differs between them, and the split parent's payee cell is NOT blank — DisplayPayeeProvider derives it from the children (packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useDisplayPayee.tsx:96-140). This is the point on which the prior plan review's stated reason is wrong.

Default confirmed in code: packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema/executors.ts:51-55 defaults the option to 'inline'; execTransactionsBasic at :238-244 appends `is_parent = 0` whenever the option is not 'all'.

Baseline suite on this checkout before any change: 143 tests across 3 files, all passing — src/server/schedules/app.test.ts (48), src/shared/schedules.test.ts (80), src/server/forecast/app.test.ts (15).

alternatives_considered.approach: Copy `schedule` and `schedule_occurrence` onto split children in makeChild, so the stamp survives on a row the default 'inline' query can see.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Changes what a split means for every schedule-linked transaction and every other consumer of children (forecast, merge, register totals), and would double-count a stamp across parent and children. getHasTransactionsQuery/getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery already read parents via splits: 'all' — so the guard, not the split model, is the outlier.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give the guard its own shared query builder in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, next to getHasTransactionsQuery, so the three occurrence queries sit together and cannot drift.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The guard's question (exact stamp match, no date fallback) is a different shape from getHasTransactionsQuery's (stamp OR a lower-bound date arm); a shared builder would either grow a switch flag or unify two queries that are deliberately different. It also spreads a one-line fix across two files. Worth revisiting only if a fourth occurrence query appears.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add an explicit is_parent/is_child check or a post-hoc filter over the 'all' result set instead of setting splits: 'all'.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Equivalent to what splits: 'all' already does, but by hand and less legibly. The sibling queries express the same intent declaratively, and matching them is what keeps the three in agreement.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the guard alone and fix the divergence on the read side instead, so the status queries also ignore split parents.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Inverts the fix in the direction the issue warns about: the Schedules page would read a genuinely paid occurrence as unpaid, the forecast row would come back, and the occurrence could then be posted for real. That turns a read-side cosmetic bug into an actual double payment.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep AC-1's original payee-count observable and reject the plan review's required restatement, on the grounds that I could not reproduce the review's evidence.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The review's evidence is indeed wrong about the payee cell, but its conclusion stands on other grounds I verified: the payee count is 1 in the collapsed register and 3 in the expanded one, so the same sentence passes or fails depending only on the expansion state the tester happens to be in. An acceptance criterion whose answer depends on unstated UI state is not observable. The Split-marker formulation the review required is stable in both states, so it is adopted — with the reason corrected rather than the requirement.

assumptions: The issue's stated fix — add .options({ splits: 'all' }) to the guard — is the intended shape, and it is correct as reproduced. No recorded decision contradicts it (plan/brief.md holds none).

'Post transaction' (no date) on the Schedules page for a ONE-OFF schedule re-dispatches the same occurrence, because a one-off's next_date never advances. Confirmed server-side on this checkout; this is what makes the browser check in AC-1 deterministic rather than dependent on recurring-date arithmetic.
QA drives the browser app at localhost:3001 with a demo budget ('View demo' on the setup screen), which is the environment .sdlc/config.yml describes.

The register's Split affordance is reached from a transaction's Category cell dropdown, as TransactionsTable.tsx:1772-1868 renders it (a CellButton labelled 'Split' in the category cell, plus a 'split' menu value at :1928).
unknowns: Not driven through a live UI: the AC-1 walkthrough was established by tracing the dispatch path, reproducing the identical handler sequence server-side, and rendering the real TransactionsTable with a persisted split — not by clicking through the running app. The render covers what the split parent displays; it does not cover the click path that creates it.

Whether a schedule split created by a RULE (execSplitActions in packages/loot-core/src/server/rules/rule.ts) leaves the stamp in the same place as one created by the UI. Both route through shared splitTransaction, so it should, but no test covers the rule-created variant and this change does not add one.
work_order.debate_summary: One judgement call dominates this replan, and it goes against the brief's stated reason. The plan review required three sites (AC-1 check, AC-1 how_to_verify, qa_script step 8) be restated in terms of the Split marker instead of counting 'one transaction for that payee and date — the split parent', on the grounds that a split parent's payee cell renders blank so the count is 0 collapsed and 2 expanded. I checked that claim by rendering the real TransactionsTable with a persisted split parent and two children: the payee cell contains the payee ('Alice'), because PayeeCell renders useDisplayPayee and DisplayPayeeProvider derives a parent's payee from its children. The review's evidence is therefore wrong, and I have said so explicitly in the understanding and the risks so nobody encodes "a split parent has a blank payee cell" in a test name or a comment. The required change is applied anyway, because its conclusion survives on different evidence I gathered myself: the Split marker is on exactly one row in BOTH the collapsed and the expanded state, while the payee is on one row collapsed and three expanded. An acceptance criterion whose answer flips with an unstated piece of UI state is not observable in the sense a QA agent needs, so the Split marker is the right observable and the review was right to demand it. The pre-split step ('confirm exactly one transaction for that payee and date') is kept as the review directed — it runs before the split, where the payee is on the row and the count is unambiguous. Nothing else in the previous plan changed: the one-line fix, its comment, the test block, the over-blocking case, the `today` exemption and the out-of-scope list all re-verified against this checkout, and the fix was applied and re-run here rather than inherited on trust.
residual_risks: Deliberately not covered: a schedule posted and split by a RULE rather than by the UI. It shares the same splitTransaction path so the guard fix covers it, but nothing asserts it, and a rule-created split that lost the stamp would re-open this bug silently.

Deliberately not covered: the stamp's lifecycle across unsplit. Unsplitting a posted-and-split transaction drops the stamp entirely, so an occurrence whose payment was split and then unsplit can be posted again — pre-existing behaviour this change neither causes nor fixes; listed in out_of_scope.

The guard is widened, not restructured. Nothing prevents a later change from widening it further (for instance to a date range), and the only thing standing between that and a missed payment is the over-blocking test in AC-2.

The browser path in AC-1 was verified by code trace plus a component render, not by clicking through a running app. If the Split affordance has moved in the UI, QA will hit that before the criterion itself is at risk.

`packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/forecast-filters.ts:83`

Evidence: Reproduced by driving the real handlers (schedule/post-transaction, then splitTransaction + transactions-batch-update) then calling generateForecast on a weekly -10000 schedule with occurrence 2017-01-02, currentDay() pinned to 2017-01-01, children carrying realistic amounts (-5000/-5000). Split case, 2017-01-02: { bal: -20000, n: 1 } — the n:1 row is PROJECTED, built by forecast-projection.ts:196-207 from scheduleOccurrencesByDay, not a real row. Control, identical setup without the split: { bal: -10000, n: 0 }. DB after the split confirms the mechanism: parent {id:'id5', is_parent:true, sched:'id2', occ:'2017-01-02'}, children {id:'id6', sched:null, occ:null} and {id:'id7', sched:null, occ:null} — the stamped row is exactly the row the inline query excludes, since execTransactionsBasic appends is_parent = 0 for anything but 'all' (aql/schema/executors.ts:238-244).

Fix: Do not read the stamp off getTransactions's result, which is inline-split for balance reasons unrelated to schedules (children carry the amounts the projection sums). Fetch occurrence state separately with the query that already exists: getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery (shared/schedules.ts:251) passes splits: 'all' and returns exactly the ['schedule','date','schedule_occurrence'] shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions/isScheduleOccurrencePosted already expect. Pass that into buildFutureScheduleOccurrences instead of transactions. This is pre-existing and display-only — it cannot cause a double payment, since that is the guard, which is fixed — so it need not block, but out_of_scope should say so; the current root_cause's 'sole outlier of the three' is true as written and misleading as read, since the stamp has four readers.

I ran q('transactions').options({ splits: 'all' }).filter({ $or: [{ id: parentId }, { parent_id: parentId }] }).select(['id', 'is_parent', 'parent_id', 'schedule_occurrence']) against a real split and it returned all three rows with the correct parent/child flags, so the helper could stay in the same idiom as every other assertion in the file.

`packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.test.ts:1566`

Evidence: AQL declares both fields the helper reaches for: parent_id at packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema/index.ts:39 and schedule_occurrence at :56, and options({ splits: 'all' }) routes through execTransactionsBasic's splitType === 'all' branch, which appends no is_parent predicate (executors.ts:238-246). I confirmed this by execution in a scratch test in this package (since removed): the query returned 3 rows for a parent plus its two children, is_parent true on the parent only. The raw form also costs the reader two things the AQL form gives for free — it hardcodes an internal view name that only executors.ts knows about, and it returns schedule_occurrence as the integer 20170102, which is why the very next assertion has to route back through AQL with the comment "Read through AQL rather than off the raw view above, which stores the occurrence as a `20170102` integer". The helper is reading the same three rows twice, in two dialects, to work around a limitation that does not exist.

Fix: Replace the body of readSplitFamily with the AQL query above (keeping the id/parent_id $or filter) and select is_parent, parent_id and schedule_occurrence. If the DbViewTransactionInternal typing gap is the real motivation, say so in the comment instead — the AQL result is typed by the schema, so the inline type literal and the internal view name both go away, as does the integer-date workaround in the assertion below.
